Synopsis:
Iceland's voters rejected restarting EU accession talks (52.8% against), leaving the government to seek alternative security arrangements. Against a backdrop of Trump's Greenland ambitions and NATO reliability concerns, Iceland's FM signals pursuit of bilateral agreements and deeper EEA cooperation. Iceland remains NATO-dependent with no standing army, anchored by a 1951 US bilateral defence pact.
